A novel / 03 / 2022

A Sea of Borrowed Names

On this coast, the sea returns everything except what you lost.

A coastal fable about inheritance, language and the stories we carry for other people.

FormatNovel / 240 imagined pages
TerritoryLanguage, inheritance, loss
StatusFictional portfolio work
Read the opening↗
01 / The story

Every winter, the tide deposits names on the shore. Some arrive on scraps of paper. Others are heard in shells. When Nera discovers her mother’s name written on a stone, she leaves the village to find the person now living under it. Her journey crosses a landscape where identity is a debt, and every introduction is a small act of faith.

“On this coast, the sea returns everything except what you lost.”
Mara Vey
Volume 03
02 / Opening passage
Original concept text

Chapter one.
Names that return

The sea brought her mother’s name back in November. It was written on a stone so smooth that Nera thought, at first, it was a piece of soap.

She carried it to the kitchen, laid it beside the bread, and waited for it to become an ordinary thing. Her grandmother kept kneading. Neither of them looked at the stone.

“There are rules,” her grandmother said at last. “For names that come back.” Outside, the gulls were arguing over something the tide had left behind.

End of sample
